newsitem.title: DENMARK: Novo to launch human hormone in US in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Novo to launch human hormone in US in 1997.

text.p: Danish pharmaceutical and biotechnological group Novo Nordisk said on Friday it planned to launch its new Nordtropin human growth hormone in the United States during the course of 1997.
"I think we can reckon that the launch will take place this year," Novo Health Care division director Lars Rebien Soerensen told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"Due to competitive considerations, we have decided at this stage not to say just when or how we will enter the U.S. market," he said.

On December 20 the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit reversed a former injunction by a lower court in an ongoing litigation patent row with rival U.S.-based Genentech, allowing Novo to go ahead and market the product in America.

"In principle the legal obstacles to our launching the product in the United States have been cleared out of the way. We are now involved in the more practical preparations for the launch," Soerensen told Reuters.
"The launch of Nordtropin will have a limited but positive affect on our American earnings, but we don't see it revolutionising our U.S. turnover," he added.
Soerensen reiterated Novo Nordisk's belief that it had not violated any patents and that its human growth hormone hormone should not be kept out of the $300 million U.S. market for such products.
Genentech went to court in a complex patent case to keep Novo's Nordtropin hormone drug off the American market, after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved the product in 1995.
Global turnover of Novo's Nordtropin drug was in 1995 around 1.5 billion crowns out of overall group earnings of 13.7 billion crowns.
